value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Vacaville/Solano County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

required_documents.notes: Directly re-read the City's own page this session; it describes what to include in the application description (system size, panel count, main service panel upgrade details) but does not itemize a formal document checklist.

value.notes: The City's own page states applicants using its Symbium-based automated platform (SB 379 compliant) 'will be able to apply for instantaneous plan review approval,' while all other photovoltaic/energy storage applications submitted via e-TRAKiT are 'subject to plan review' with 'permit processing [taking] approximately 1-3 business days, depending on staff availability.' The 0-3 day range reflects instant issuance for the Symbium-eligible pathway and up to 3 business days for the standard pathway.

value.program_or_pathway: Symbium automated permitting platform (SB 379 compliant, launched September 2023)
